Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to opt for an alternative version of the App Tracking Transparency system prompt in the European Union, as part of a recent agreement between Apple and the EU. Here are the details.

The new prompt will be mandatory in select European countries

A few weeks ago, Apple confirmed it would comply with the EU's "fairer" App Tracking Transparency rules, following an investigation into the matter by Germany's Federal Cartel Office.

The agreement brings to a close a multi-year antitrust probe aimed at determining whether Apple's ATT rules placed third-party apps at an unfair competitive disadvantage relative to Apple's own services. Apple has consistently denied the allegations, claiming it has applied equally strict privacy principles to its own apps all along. German regulators, however, were not convinced.

Apple ultimately agreed to eight changes to its ATT framework in Europe, which you can read more about here.

Apple confirmed today that iOS 27 will allow developers to opt for an "alternative App Tracking Transparency system prompt in the EU," adding that "for legal reasons, apps distributed in Germany, France, Italy, Poland, and Romania must use only this alternative version of the system prompt."

The company added that EU developers will also be able to re-prompt users one year after the user last made an ATT choice, regardless of whether they originally accepted or denied tracking.
